source.title: On some open problems about marcus contextual languages

trace.notes: Input URL normalized as a zbMATH bibliographic resolver record. Direct zbMATH page access returned a Cloudflare challenge, so identifier-specific metadata recovery was used.

zbMATH API record 3984602 resolved to DOI 10.1080/00207168508803447 and identifier 0608.68064, but zbMATH title fields were unavailable due to license restrictions. The record is bibliographic metadata and was not used as technical extraction evidence.

Crossref DOI metadata identified the exact work as "On some open problems about marcus contextual languages", International Journal of Computer Mathematics 17(1), 1985, pages 9-23, with publisher PDF candidate http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/00207168508803447 and DOI landing page https://doi.org/10.1080/00207168508803447.
OpenAlex metadata for DOI 10.1080/00207168508803447 reported open_access.is_oa=false, oa_status=closed, best_oa_location=null, and any_repository_has_fulltext=false.
Failure modes classified as blocked_or_challenged for zbMATH and Taylor & Francis routes, paywalled_or_restricted for the publisher/DOI route, and metadata_only for resolver and bibliography pages.

Ran exact-work recovery attempts using the DOI, exact title, and exact title plus PDF. Inspected candidate pages for Taylor & Francis, Academia Europaea publication list, the author's IMAR publication list, and the Romanian Academy biographical PDF. The non-publisher candidates only list the citation; the publisher route did not expose readable article full text in this environment.

No readable PDF or full HTML source containing the article's problem statements was recovered. The workflow forbids extracting questions from metadata, abstracts, citation lists, search snippets, or resolver records, so no candidates were accepted.
Saved final JSON to outputs/parse-paper/3984602.json and outputs/latest.json.
